purpose: Inspect the real state surfaces of installed Excel and Blender before building a semantic cross-application bridge.

activities.label: observe real Excel COM and Blender Python capability surfaces without mutation
attack mutation input capture camera network and write boundaries
record native state adapter decision and semantic bridge unknowns

queries.expression: do installed Excel and Blender expose observable native state surfaces without user-data mutation
is UIA alone sufficient or must the bridge combine UIA with native application APIs
does the inventory remain read-only and local
is the real-app inventory reproducible through the FARMAKSIA suite

assumptions: Excel is installed and exposes a local COM automation server on the test machine.
Blender is installed under the standard Blender Foundation directory or is supplied through --blender.
Launching Excel hidden and Blender in background factory-startup mode does not open or modify user files.
Native APIs are observation surfaces; they do not by themselves authorize future actions.
The shared bridge should preserve typed state transitions rather than force a one-to-one control mapping.
kill_tests: Excel cell or workbook mutation is blocked.
Mouse or keyboard injection is blocked.
Network, screenshot and camera capabilities are blocked.
A surface layer other than the adopted UIA boundary is rejected by the adversarial fixture.
unknowns: Whether UIA can expose enough Blender viewport semantics for a useful surface descriptor.
Whether the Excel and Blender native state graphs contain task invariants that transfer for a concrete task.
Whether future actions can be independently verified through a second state source.
Whether Excel version and subscription features are stable enough to be treated as capabilities rather than assumptions.
